\section{Actual scalar energy and its full finite-energy space}
Here is the scalar construction used in the target theorem. Represent a
rational model obstacle $f_D$ on a smooth equivariant modification
$Y\to X\times\mathbb P^1$, with full central fiber $F=\sum b_EE$ and
vertical $D$, so $f_D(v_E)=d_E/b_E$. Choose $aF\leq D\leq bF$.
Proper normal birational section descent identifies its relative full
section lattice, with $R_m=H^0(X,mL)$, as
\[
 t^{-ma}R_m[t]\subset\Lambda_m\subset t^{-mb}R_m[t],\quad
 \Lambda_m=\bigoplus_j t^{-w_{mj}}k[t]s_{mj},\quad ma\leq w_{mj}\leq mb.
\]
The last equality follows by a basis adapted to the finite homogeneous
flag, not finite generation of the whole section ring. Gluing to the
product lattice at infinity gives
\[
 h^0(Y,m(\rho_X^*L+D+cF))=\sum_j\max(w_{mj}+mc+1,0).
\]
For fixed rational $c>-a$, actual section-volume limits give
\[
 \vol_Y(\rho_X^*L+D+cF)=(n+1)cV+(n+1)\mathscr E(f_D).
\tag{5.1}
\]
The intercept is the limit of $n!m^{-n-1}\sum_jw_{mj}$. Refining models
preserves the actual lattice. It is monotone, $V$-translation equivariant,
and $V$-Lipschitz for the original sup norm. Volume-root concavity on
fixed big algebraic classes, expanded at $c\to\infty$ in (5.1), gives
concavity of this intercept on rational model functions. Uniform model
density gives its unique concave monotone $V$-Lipschitz extension to $C(K)$.

This extension is also the actual full-section trace. For $0\ne s\in R_m$
put $W_m(f;s)=\inf_K(mf-\log\|s\|)$; at section zeros the bracket is
$+\infty$. Its values lie in $[m\min f,m f(v_0)]$. Upper-weight spaces
are linear by the ultrametric inequality and their endpoints are closed.
A finite flag therefore gives an adapted basis with trace
\[
 e_m(f)=n!m^{-n-1}\sum_j\lfloor W_m(f;s_{mj})\rfloor.
\tag{5.2}
\]
For model obstacles these floors are exactly the lattice weights above.
For arbitrary continuous $f,g$ flag comparison gives
$|e_m(f)-e_m(g)|\leq(n!\dim R_m/m^n)(\|f-g\|_\infty+1/m)$.
Thus (5.2) converges to $\mathscr E(f)$ in cofinal admissible degrees.

Define on the entire actual cone
\[
 E(u)=\inf_{f\in C(K),\ f\geq u}\mathscr E(f),\qquad
 \E^1(\theta)=\{u\in\PSH(\theta):E(u)>-\infty\}.
\tag{5.3}
\]
For every section $s$, a weighted section scalar lies below $f$ iff it
lies below $P_\theta(f)$. Hence its full weights for these two obstacles
are identical. If $g\in C(K)$ dominates $P_\theta(f)$, weight monotonicity
gives $\mathscr E(g)\geq\mathscr E(f)$. Taking the outer infimum proves
$E(P_\theta(f))=\mathscr E(f)$. In particular
\[
 E(R)=0,\quad E(u+c)=E(u)+cV,
 \quad B(u):=-E(u)\geq0\text{ for }u(v_0)=0.
\]
These formulas use section volume, not $L^n$ in a nonnef class.

Extend (5.3) to all upper bounded usc obstacles. If $u_i\downarrow u$
and $f\geq u$ is continuous, compactness of
$\{u_i\geq f+\epsilon\}$ gives a tail $u_i<f+\epsilon$. Monotonicity
then gives $\inf_i E(u_i)\leq\mathscr E(f)+\epsilon V$.
Taking the outer infimum proves decreasing-net energy continuity,
including $-\infty$. Continuous majorant nets of two usc obstacles,
their sums, and continuous concavity give concavity of the outer extension
and hence of $E$ on the genuine cone. The genuine floors
$\max(u,R-N)$ decrease all-point to normalized $u$ and have costs at
most $NV$. Their decreasing energies characterize all of (5.3); no bounded
relative-singularity restriction replaces this space.

This section constructs scalar energy, not a mixed unbounded operator.
In particular a polar physical complete-system function is not put into
$\E^1$ by its moving decomposition. Even for $\OO(1)$ on $\mathbb P^1$,
the floors of $\log\|z_1\|$ have energy $-N/2$, so its energy is
$-\infty$ by G0. The common horizontal factor used later is only a
literal section identity.

\section{Capped divisors, a genuine finite-energy pole, and targets}
Let $D\geq0$ be an actual integral Cartier divisor and
$a_D=-\log\|s_D\|\in[0,+\infty]$. Its caps are ordinary continuous.
For rational $t>0$ with $L-tD$ big, and integer $N\geq1$, set
\[
 f_{t,N}=-\min(t a_D,N),\qquad u_{t,N}=P_\theta(f_{t,N}).
\]
The minorant $R-N$ ensures genuine existence. In denominator-cleared
degrees the actual injection
\[
 s_D^{mt}:H^0(X,m(L-tD))\hookrightarrow H^0(X,mL)
\]
has every nonzero image vector of full obstacle weight zero. Indeed
$\log\|s' s_D^{mt}\|\leq-mt a_D\leq m f_{t,N}$ everywhere, with literal
$-\infty\leq-mN$ at supported zeros, and equality at $v_0$. All other
weights lie in $[-mN,0]$. An adapted basis retains at least
$h^0(m(L-tD))$ zero weights. Flooring and section-volume limits prove
\[
 0\leq B(u_{t,N})\leq N[\vol(L)-\vol(L-tD)].
\tag{6.1}
\]
The same image section is a genuine minorant of generic value zero, so
$u_{t,N}$ is normalized without a shift altering its cap. It satisfies
$R-N\leq u_{t,N}\leq R$ and $u_{t,N}\leq-N$ on $D^{\rm an}$.
The cap can also be represented as a rational model function: for
$t=a/b$, use $\OO(-aD)+(\tau^{bN})$ on $X\times\mathbb A^1$ and scale
its ideal model function by $1/b$. No approximation of supported poles
by finite valuations changes the calculation.

Choose $\lambda_j=2^{-j}$, $N_j=4^j$, and rational $t_j$ small enough that
$L-t_jD$ is big and $N_j[V-\vol(L-t_jD)]\leq2^{-j}$.
Volume continuity is used inside the big cone, with $N_j$ fixed first.
The actual convex functions
\[
 w_q=\sum_{j\leq q}\lambda_j u_{t_j,N_j}+2^{-q}R
\]
are normalized and decrease all-point. Concavity gives $E(w_q)\geq-1/3$.
The closure and energy continuity proved above give a genuine
$w_D\in\E^1(\theta)$ with $E(w_D)\geq-1/3$. On the entire original
$D^{\rm an}$ it is $-\infty$, since
$w_q\leq-\sum_{j\leq q}2^j$. This verifies the convex-series and
normalization steps proposed in Root197.

An intrinsic target here is a positive Radon measure of raw mass $V$ with
\[
 \nu\{R=-\infty\}=0,\qquad
 I_\nu(u):=\int(R-u)\,d\nu<\infty
 \quad\text{for every normalized actual }u\in\E^1(\theta).
\tag{6.2}
\]
The difference uses actual values where $R$ is finite. Applying (6.2) to
$w_D$ gives $\nu(D^{\rm an}\setminus\{R=-\infty\})=0$; the first
condition handles the rest. Every proper algebraic closed subset lies
in an actual divisor: twist its ideal by a sufficiently large actual
ample power and take a nonzero section. Hence every target (6.2) is
algebraically null. No absolute integrability of $R$ was used.
If one specifies finite intrinsic dual energy
\[
 D_\nu=\sup_{u(v_0)=0}\{E(u)+I_\nu(u)\}<\infty,
\tag{6.3}
\]
it directly implies (6.2) because every finite-energy cost is finite.
Conversely proving full equivalence and coercivity would use a
relative-contraction estimate; such a transfer is not an inverse equation.
The nullness conclusion alone does not concern all nonalgebraic polar or
negligible sets, nor continuity on varying weakly convergent tests.

\section{Corrected finite-nef identities and an ordered energy-gap bound}
On any fixed actual nef generic rational bundle $A$ let $T_\xi=(A,\xi)$
for a bounded relatively nef model scalar. Finite mixed model products
are positive, of raw mass $V_A=A^n$, and keep coefficients
$b_E(T|_E)^n$. Define $e_A(\xi)=T_\xi^{n+1}/(n+1)$ and
$J_A(\xi)=\xi(v_0)V_A-e_A(\xi)$, and
\[
 \|f\|_{T_1\cdots T_{n-1}}^2=-(0,f)^2T_1\cdots T_{n-1}\geq0,
 \quad d_A(\xi,\eta)=\max_{j<n}\|\xi-\eta\|_{T_\xi^jT_\eta^{n-1-j}}^2.
\]
Vertical Hodge and Cauchy--Schwarz are finite algebraic facts; adding
actual ample slots and taking their finite polynomial limits is another
justification through G0. No unbounded nonample estimate is invoked.

For $S=(0,\xi-\eta)$, two telescoping sums give exactly
\[
 T_\eta^{n+1}-T_\xi^{n+1}+(n+1)S T_\eta^n
 =-\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}(n-j)S^2T_\xi^jT_\eta^{n-1-j}.
\tag{7.1}
\]
For each $j$ the summand occurs for $k=j+1,\ldots,n$. In particular
\[
 J_A(\xi)=\frac1{n+1}\sum_{j<n}(n-j)\|\xi\|_{T_\xi^jT_0^{n-1-j}}^2.
\tag{7.2}
\]
The order $j+1$ with these factors is false. On
$\operatorname{Bl}_{(p,0)}(\mathbb P^2\times\mathbb P^1)$ take
$T_\xi=H-aE$, $0<a<1$. The actual relatively ample model has
$H^3=H^2E=HE^2=0$, $E^3=1$. Thus
$J=a^3/3$, $\|\xi\|_{T_0}^2=0$, $\|\xi\|_{T_\xi}^2=a^3$;
the erroneous order gives $2a^3/3$. This is a proof-level intersection
witness; the accompanying finite arithmetic only checks transcription.

\begin{lemma}[Ordered finite-model gap]\label{gap}
If $\xi\geq\eta$ on the fixed carrier, then
\[
 d_A(\xi,\eta)\leq n(n+1)[e_A(\xi)-e_A(\eta)].
\tag{7.3}
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Write $\Delta=e_A(\xi)-e_A(\eta)$. The energy difference is
\[
 \Delta=\frac1{n+1}\sum_{k=0}^n
 \int(\xi-\eta)\,T_\xi^kT_\eta^{n-k}.
\]
Every summand is nonnegative and each endpoint integral is at most
$(n+1)\Delta$. The tangent remainder in (7.1), divided by $n+1$, is
$-\Delta+\int(\xi-\eta)d\MA_A(\eta)\leq n\Delta$.
Its coefficient of each seminorm is at least $1/(n+1)$.
This proves (7.3). No generic normalization or division by $V_A$ is needed.
\end{proof}

For completeness the corrected finite slot-change argument gives
\[
 \|\xi-\xi'\|_{T_\psi^jT_0^{n-1-j}}^2
 \leq C_n d_A(\xi,\xi')^{2^{1-n}}
       \max\{J_A(\xi),J_A(\xi'),J_A(\psi)\}^{1-2^{1-n}}.
\tag{7.4}
\]
Here is the proof structure needed to fix its scope. Average slots show
$d_A(\xi,\xi')\asymp_n\|\xi-\xi'\|_{T_{(\xi+\xi')/2}^{n-1}}^2$.
The tangent remainder in (7.1) is comparable to $d_A$ and convex in its
first potential. Put $f=\xi-\xi'$, $\tau=(\xi+\xi')/2$,
$a=d_A(\xi,\xi')$, $b=\max(d_A(\xi,\eta),d_A(\xi',\eta))$ and
$b_j=\|f\|_{T_\eta^jT_\tau^{n-1-j}}^2$. Then $b_0\leq C_na$ and
$b_{n-1}\leq4b$. Replacing one slot, splitting the second $f$ into
$T_\xi-T_{\xi'}$, and using Cauchy--Schwarz with
$T_\xi,T_{\xi'}\leq2T_\tau$ gives
$b_{j+1}-b_j\leq C_n\sqrt{b_j b}$. If $a\leq b$, induction gives
$b_j\leq C_n a^{2^{-j}}b^{1-2^{-j}}$; if $a>b$ use $b_{n-1}\leq4b$.
Apply this bound through a third potential to derive
$d\leq C_n b^{2^{1-n}}\max(d,b)^{1-2^{1-n}}$; solving it proves
the quasi-triangle bound. Average arbitrary nef slots, expand the
nonnegative multinomial terms, use this bound, and (7.2); this proves
(7.4). For $n=1$ the empty-slot seminorm gives the result directly.

With $\alpha=2^{-n}$, telescoping the $n$th powers from $j=0$ and
applying (7.4) and Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
 \left|\int(\xi-\eta)d\MA_A(\psi)
       -(\xi(v_0)-\eta(v_0))V_A\right|
 \leq C_n d_A(\xi,\eta)^\alpha J_A(\psi)^{1/2}
       M^{1/2-\alpha},
\tag{7.5}
\]
where $M=\max(J_A(\xi),J_A(\eta),J_A(\psi))$.
Indeed each $\psi$ seminorm in that sum is at most
$d_A(\psi,0)^{1/2}$, and each difference seminorm is bounded by
the square root of (7.4). Equations (7.3)--(7.5) are the proposed
ordered-gap refinement, rather than a bound only in terms of the test's
total energy. They hold also when $A^n=0$: all raw positive top measures
then vanish, and no probability normalization appears.

\section{Conditional gap transfer, uniform collars, and all-test tails}
All assertions in this section assume F, in addition to the earlier
proved scalar foundations. We give the actual measure passage.

For fixed normalized model envelopes $a=P(f_H)\geq b=P(f_J)$ from
ordered obstacles, and normalized model output base $w=P(f_D)$, F2,
Lemma \ref{gap}, and (7.5) imply
\[
 \int(a-b)\,dM(w)
 \leq C_n[E(a)-E(b)]^\alpha B(w)^{1/2}
       \max\{B(a),B(b),B(w)\}^{1/2-\alpha}.
\tag{9.1}
\]
The generic difference error is retained at each finite moving stage and
vanishes only after $m\to\infty$. To justify identifying its left side,
one can subtract the two bounded relative section-quotient integrals.
Their endpoint envelopes and reference are continuous off $Z$ by (4.3).
The original output $M(w)$ is finite divisorial and misses $Z$.
Fixed-degree bounds
\[
 \max(-C,\phi_{q,H}-R)\leq\phi_{m,H}-\phi_{m,0}
 \leq\min(C,a-\phi_{q,0})
\]
are respectively lsc and usc near these atoms. They converge there to
$a-R$ by (4.3). A continuous cutoff equal to one on their finite support
and supported in the finite-stage open set allows Radon-net
semicontinuity to squeeze the full integral. The omitted measure mass
tends to zero by weak convergence and the cutoff. This proves the
bounded weighted identification without uniform quotient convergence
and without subtracting supported infinities. The same argument applies
to $b-R$. Thus (9.1) follows with no atomic support assumption on the
domain of the ultimate output $M(u)$.

For each actual effective divisor $S$ there is a uniform algebraic collar
estimate, stronger than pointwise algebraic nullness. Put
$a_S=-\log\|s_S\|$. On a fixed determination of $S$ and fixed ample
$T$, choose $d$ with $dT-\rho_X^*S$ nef. For $D\leq0$ and fixed $c>B/V$,
write $\gamma=\rho_X^*L+cF$. The vertical part of the pulled $S$ has
coefficients $b_Ev_E(s_S)$. Its horizontal remainder is effective;
the ordinary volume derivative in each effective direction is nonnegative.
Positive-product order paired with the fixed nef test gives
\[
 \int a_S\,d\mu_{D,c}
 \leq\langle(\rho_X^*L+D+cF)^n\rangle\cdot\rho_X^*S
 \leq d\langle\gamma^n\rangle\cdot T=:C_{c,S}.
\]
F3's positive tail implies, for the original continuous cap,
\[
 \int\min(a_S,N)\,d\mu_D\leq C_{c,S}+NB/c.
\tag{9.2}
\]
F1 passes (9.2) to every $M(u)$ with $B(u)\leq B$. Consequently
\[
 \sup_{B(u)\leq B}M(u)\{a_S\geq N\}
 \leq C_{c,S}/N+B/c.
\tag{9.3}
\]
First choose $c$, then $N$. Letting $N\to\infty$ and then
$c\to\infty$ also proves $M(u)(S^{\rm an})=0$. The fixed determination
and its nef test precede every model or measure limit. This argument
uses no signed positive-product monotonicity.

Every bounded continuous function on $K\setminus Z$, with bounded
Borel extension elsewhere, has converging integrals under a weak net
of these outputs converging to an algebraically null limit. To see it,
use a continuous cutoff $\chi_N$ equal to one for $a_{E_0}\leq N$ and
zero for $a_{E_0}\geq2N$. The product extends continuously by zero,
since it vanishes on a neighborhood of $Z$. For a fixed limiting measure
ordinary Radon regularity makes the collar error small; (9.3) makes it
uniform on bounded-cost output families. The continuous integral passes
through weak convergence with this fixed collar. This proves bounded
relative integral convergence for all the model envelopes in (9.1).
It follows that (9.1) holds with $w$ replaced by every normalized
genuine output base $u\in\E^1$, by F1 and a fixed test pair.

Let $v_i=P(f_i)\downarrow v$ be normalized nonpositive model-majorant
envelopes of any $v\in\E^1$. For fixed $i$ use (9.1) on $v_i\geq v_j$,
then $j\to\infty$ with the output fixed. Monotone convergence on the
algebraically null complement gives
\[
 \int(v_i-v)\,dM(u)\leq
 C_n[E(v_i)-E(v)]^\alpha B(u)^{1/2}
       \max\{B(v),B(u)\}^{1/2-\alpha}.
\tag{9.4}
\]
Every difference is defined where $R$ is finite. Taking $i$ to the
zero obstacle first also gives the usual all-$\E^1$ relative moment
bound, with $B(v)^\alpha$ instead of the energy gap. Formula (9.4)
is the new approximation-tail bound: it tends to zero uniformly over
all outputs $B(u)\leq B$, for each fixed finite-energy test $v$.
For $n=1$ its last exponent is zero; the expression is read as
$C_1[E(v_i)-E(v)]^{1/2}B(u)^{1/2}$, including zero cases by continuity.

Fix such a family and $\epsilon>0$. Choose $i$ so its (9.4) error is
small. The bounded nonnegative function $R-v_i$ is continuous off $Z$,
with norm at most $C_i$. Fix $c$, then $N$ using (9.3), so its omitted
collar cost is small for this $C_i$. The actual original function
\[
 b=\chi_N(R-v_i)\text{ off }Z,\qquad b=0\text{ near }Z,
\tag{9.5}
\]
belongs to $C(K)$, is nonnegative, and obeys
\[
 \sup_{B(u)\leq B}\int|(R-v)-b|\,dM(u)<\epsilon.
\tag{9.6}
\]
Indeed the absolute error is bounded by
$v_i-v+(1-\chi_N)(R-v_i)$. Thus this is an absolute $L^1$ assertion
for an original continuous approximant, with the test index and polar
collar fixed before any output index. This also proves uniform integrable
tails for the fixed test over the output family: if $C=\|b\|_\infty$,
then $(R-v)\mathbf1_{\{R-v>2C\}}\leq2|(R-v)-b|$.
A bounded first-moment bound alone would not have implied it.
For a single fixed intrinsic target
(6.2), dominated convergence and its algebraic nullness give a small
error for the same construction after making $i,N$ sufficiently large;
this does not make the assertion uniform on arbitrary varying tests
against that target.

\section{Conditional weighted continuity and entire supporting planes}
Continue to assume F. The test-net ordering issue can be resolved without

$\phi_{m,f}\leq\phi_{m',f}$ for $m\mid m'$.
Degrees are directed by divisibility, with denominators cleared;
no countability assumption on the field or defining FS net is used.

\begin{theorem}\label{density}
For every $f\in C(K)$,
\[
                  u_f(x)=\sup_m\phi_{m,f}(x)
                    \quad(x\in U).                    \tag{3}
\]
The value is finite continuous on $U$, and the cofinal stages converge
uniformly on every compact subset of $U$. Equality on $Z$ is not claimed.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The envelope exists because $R-C\leq-C\leq f$. Monotonicity and
constant shifts give $R-C\leq u_f\leq R+C$.
Tensor the section of $E_0$ with a full generated power of $aA$.
It gives an actual FS potential $W$ on $L$, and $W-C\leq f$.
Hence $u_f$ is finite on $U$.

Take a defining FS net $h_i\downarrow u_f$ on actual $M_i$.
Fix $\epsilon>0$. Compactness gives eventually $h_i\leq f+\epsilon$
\emph{on all of $K$}. Indeed the closed sets
$\{h_i\geq f+\epsilon\}$ decrease and have empty intersection,
since their all-point limit is at most $f$. This uses a continuous
obstacle and a strict margin, including at old poles.

Fix rational $t\in(0,1)$ before taking a late defining stage. The
actual rational bundle
\[
                B_{i,t}=L-(1-t)M_i-t(L-aA)               \tag{4}
\]
is eventually ample since its numerical class tends to $ta[A]$.
After clearing powers, its full generated FS system is identically
zero on the entire original carrier: some section is a unit at the
center of each semivaluation, including a supported one.
Tensor the actual FS stages and this generated factor. The scalar
\[
                g_{i,t,\epsilon}
                    =(1-t)(h_i-\epsilon)+t(W-C)          \tag{5}
\]
is an actual FS function on $L$, with all tensor exponents cleared.
No numerical bundle equality is substituted for (4). Because
$h_i-\epsilon\leq f$ and $W-C\leq-C\leq f$, (5) is below $f$
on the entire carrier. In particular it is a genuine minorant.

Any actual FS minorant $g$ of $f$ is below the supremum in (3).
To verify this with real weights, write
$g=r^{-1}\max_j(\log|s_j|+\lambda_j)$ on an actual power of $L$.
The minorant inequalities imply $W_r(f;s_j)\geq\lambda_j$.
Raise each section to the $\ell$th power; in degree $r\ell$ its
weight is at least $\ell\lambda_j$. The corresponding integer part
loses less than one. Thus
$\phi_{r\ell,f}\geq g-1/(r\ell)$; basis independence just proved
allows use of each of these sections. Let $\ell\to\infty$.

For $x\in U$, $W(x)$ and $u_f(x)$ are finite. Apply this observation
to (5), take the defining tail $i$, then let rational $t\downarrow0$
and finally $\epsilon\downarrow0$. It proves the reverse inequality
in (3); the upper inequality was already proved.

The full section system of one fixed cofinal degree is finite on all
of $U$, by the same Kodaira-section tensor with a generated ample
factor. Since $|f|\leq C$, every filtration weight is in
$[-mC,mC]$, and $\phi_{m,f}\geq\phi_{m,0}-C$; here the integer
choice of $C$ removes any rounding error in this bound. Therefore
all cofinal stages after that degree are finite continuous on $U$.
Their supremum is lsc, and the genuine envelope is usc. Equality (3)
makes it continuous there. On a compact $F\subset U$ the continuous
nonnegative gaps $u_f-\phi_{m,f}$ decrease to zero. Their closed
positive-margin superlevels have empty intersection, so compactness
gives uniform convergence. This is the Dini argument for the
divisibility-directed stages, rather than a metrizability assumption.
\end{proof}

For $f=0$, (3) recovers the reference assertion. For a bounded rational
model obstacle $f_H$, its full time lattice is exactly (1) with cleared
denominators, when the ordinary section-lattice identification has
been reconstructed. Thus the density theorem gives both the reference
and the test-envelope equalities on $U$, instead of assuming a
general negligible-set theorem. It does not give below-approximants
for an arbitrary unbounded obstacle.

\section{Fixed continuous approximants with absolute integral errors}
Write $u=u_f$ and $b=u-R$ on $U$. Monotonicity gives $|b|\leq C$,
and Theorem~\ref{density} makes $b$ continuous on $U$.
Let positive Radon measures $\nu_i\to\nu$ weakly on $K$, with
converging finite masses. Assume $\nu(Z)=0$.
Let $m_i$ tend cofinally in admissible divisibility degrees. Suppose
bounded measurable tests $a_i$ on the supports of $\nu_i$ satisfy
$|a_i|\leq C$ and, wherever both terms are finite,
\[
                  a_i=\phi_{m_i,f}-\phi_{m_i,0}.          \tag{6}
\]
The equality is required on each compact subset of $U$ for all
sufficiently late $i$. It need not define a subtraction at common poles.

\begin{theorem}\label{weighted}
For every $\eta>0$ there is an actual $B\in C(K)$, $|B|\leq C$, with
\[
 \int_U|b-B|\,d\nu<\eta,\qquad
 \int|a_i-B|\,d\nu_i<\eta\quad\text{eventually}.          \tag{7}
\]
Consequently $\int a_i\,d\nu_i\to\int_U(u_f-R)\,d\nu$.
The compact collar and $B$ are fixed before the degree and measure
indices tend to their limits. There is no atomic-support hypothesis.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
If $\nu(K)=0$, take $B=0$ and use $\nu_i(K)\to0$.
Otherwise let $M>\nu(K)$ bound all sufficiently late masses.
Radon inner regularity and $\nu(U)=\nu(K)$ give a compact
$F\subset U$ whose omitted mass is arbitrarily small. Choose
$0\leq\chi\leq1$ continuous, equal to one on $F$, with support
contained in $U$. Its compact support is a fixed collar away from $Z$.
Define $B=\chi b$ on $U$ and zero outside $U$. It is continuous
on $K$: $b$ is bounded and the support of $\chi$ stays inside $U$.
Its limiting error is at most $C\int(1-\chi)\,d\nu$.

Theorem~\ref{density} gives uniform convergence of both section stages
on $\operatorname{supp}\chi$. Fix one degree $q$ after their
individual errors there are at most $\delta>0$. For $m_i$ sufficiently
divisible and large, their monotonicity and envelope upper bounds give
$|a_i-b|\leq2\delta$ on this fixed support. On the full measure support,
\[
                   |a_i-B|\leq2\delta\chi+C(1-\chi).
                                                        \tag{8}
\]
Outside the collar (8) uses only $|a_i|\leq C$; no value of $b$
at a reference pole is required. First choose the compact collar
so the limiting omitted integral is small, then $\delta$ with
$2\delta M$ small, and finally this fixed $q$. Weak convergence of
the masses and of the continuous $\chi$ gives (7) with room in the
strict inequalities. Integrating $B$ and using (7) proves the limit.
\end{proof}

\section{Actual moving-model application and its limits}
For a fixed bounded rational model obstacle $f_H$, suppose its
complete relative stages and the zero stages share the actual generic
moving factor $T_m$:
\[
 \phi_{m,H}\circ p_m^{\mathrm{an}}=q_{T_m}+\psi_{m,H},
 \qquad\phi_{m,0}\circ p_m^{\mathrm{an}}=q_{T_m}.
                                                        \tag{9}
\]
Time-lattice comparison gives $|\psi_{m,H}|\leq C$.
Suppose the actual pushed auxiliary nef measures converge weakly

At their function-field divisorial atoms, the horizontal factor is
finite and the valuative birational lift is unique; hence their

Algebraic nullness of general outer-energy outputs is a separate

\title{Approximating every intrinsic target by actual outputs\protect\\

\author{Unreviewed conditional research, continuation 199}

\begin{document}
\maketitle
\begin{abstract}
Under the explicit genuine scalar, output and uniform variation
foundations, every intrinsic finite-dual-energy target is a weak limit
of outputs of normalized model-envelope near maximizers with bounded
energy costs. This conclusion uses approximate stationarity before
any maximizer is known to exist. We first justify model approximation
of the objective using Radon regularity for directed continuous costs;
ordinary measurable monotone convergence cannot simply be applied
to arbitrary nets. Uniform model variation extends to every genuine
base with the same constants. If the separate ordered-gap tail package
holds, every fixed genuine finite-energy test also has converging
relative integrals along the output approximants. These are conditional
bridges, and neither variational attainment nor the full inverse
equation is claimed.
\end{abstract}

\section{Actual domain and the precise unproved foundations}
Retain every smooth integral projective $n$-fold, $n\geq1$, over every
algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, and
every actual big rational bundle $L$. Put $K=X^{\mathrm{an}}$,
$\theta=c_1(L)$, $V=\operatorname{vol}(L)>0$, and let $v_0$ be the
generic trivial valuation. All supported semivaluations remain on $K$.
The genuine cone consists of actual functions obtained from one
all-point decreasing FS net on varying actual rational bundles with
classes tending to $\theta$ and a finite generic endpoint.
No abstract energy completion, countability or probability division
replaces these data.

The following are explicit conditional inputs. They have been proposed
in the unreviewed partial papers; their historical status supplies no
theorem grant.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The genuine cone is convex and decreasing closed, with actual
obstacle envelopes whenever there is a genuine minorant. Its normalized
reference $R=P_\theta(0)$ satisfies $R(v_0)=0$ and $u\leq R$ for
normalized $u$. The raw section energy is concave, monotone and
decreasing continuous, with $E(R)=0$ and $E(u+c)=E(u)+cV$.
Write $B(u)=-E(u)$ for normalized genuine $u\in\EE$.
Every such $u$ has nonpositive rational model majorants
$f_i\downarrow u$, $f_i(v_0)=0$, whose genuine envelopes
$u_i=P_\theta(f_i)$ decrease to $u$ with $E(u_i)\downarrow E(u)$.
For fixed $h\in C(K)$ their perturbed envelopes decrease to
$P_\theta(u+th)$ for each fixed $t$.
\item One actual Kodaira divisor $Z=E_0^{\mathrm{an}}$ has open
complement $U$. The reference and every bounded continuous-obstacle
envelope are finite continuous on $U$. There is a genuine normalized
$w_Z\in\EE$ with $w_Z=-\infty$ on $Z$.
For some dimension constant $C_n\geq1$, the genuine contraction obeys
\[
 B((1-r)R+ru)\leq C_n r^2 B(u),\qquad0<r<1.                 \tag{1}
\]
\item A target-independent map $M$ has positive original Radon
outputs of raw mass $V$ on all genuine $\EE$. At a model envelope
it equals its finite divisorial volume-derivative measure. For the
canonical majorants in item1, $M(u_i)\to M(u)$ weakly.
All outputs give $Z$ zero mass.
\item The proposed uniform finite-model Taylor estimate is valid.
For a fixed rational model direction $h$, a cost bound $B$, and
$c>B/V$, there are $K_c<\infty$ and $t_c>0$, independent of the
nonpositive model obstacle and its refinement, such that
\[
 \left|\mathscr E(f+th)-\mathscr E(f)
                -t\int h\,dM(P_\theta(f))\right|
 \leq K_ct^2/2+|t|A_h(B)/c,\qquad |t|<t_c,                 \tag{2}
\]
when $f(v_0)=0$ and $B(P_\theta(f))\leq B$.
Here $\mathscr E(f)=E(P_\theta(f))$ and one may use
$A_h(B)=\|h\|_\infty(2B+2V\|h\|_\infty)$.
Rational model functions are uniformly dense in the original $C(K)$.
\end{enumerate}
Items1--4 are the antecedents of the approximation theorem below.
In particular (2) is stronger than pointwise volume differentiability.
Its proposed proof uses deficient positive measures with tail mass
$\leq B/c$, and fixed signed Cartier tests paired through two fixed
nef tests on actual big smooth algebraic determinations. Those proofs
remain to be independently audited. Neither an ample unbounded
estimate nor an inverse equation is assumed here.

Let $\nu$ be any positive original Radon target of mass $V$ with
literal reference-pole exclusion, all relative finite-energy costs
finite, and finite intrinsic dual energy:
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \nu\{R=-\infty\}=0,\quad
 I_\nu(u)=\int(R-u)\,d\nu<\infty\ (u(v_0)=0),\\
 D_\nu=\sup_{u\in\EE,\ u(v_0)=0}\{E(u)+I_\nu(u)\}<\infty.
 \end{gathered}                                             \tag{3}
\]
Relative values are actual differences where $R$ is finite.
The existence of $w_Z$ implies $\nu(Z)=0$: its cost is infinite
on $Z$ outside reference poles, and the latter are already excluded.
No absolute integrability of $R$ is needed. The earlier capped-section
rank construction proposes $w_Z$ in precisely this genuine space.

\section{Directed continuous costs and near maximizers}
\begin{lemma}[Radon convergence for the actual directed costs]\label{radon}
Let $c_i$ be a directed increasing net of nonnegative continuous
functions on $U$, and let $\nu$ be finite Radon on $K$, $\nu(Z)=0$.
Then $\int_U\sup_i c_i\,d\nu=\sup_i\int_U c_i\,d\nu$,
with $+\infty$ permitted.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For $a>0$, $\{\sup_i c_i>a\}=\bigcup_i\{c_i>a\}$ is open in $U$.
Every compact subset of this union has a finite subcover by these
open superlevels, and directedness gives one index dominating that
finite set of indices. Radon inner regularity therefore gives
\[
 \nu\{\sup_i c_i>a\}=\sup_i\nu\{c_i>a\}.
\]
For any finite collection of thresholds the corresponding masses can
be approached simultaneously by one index. Apply this fact to the
finite lower step sums for the layer-cake integral of
$\min(\sup_i c_i,N)$. Then refine the threshold mesh and send
$N\to\infty$. It proves the nontrivial inequality; the other follows
from $c_i\leq\sup_jc_j$. This argument uses Radon regularity and
continuity, rather than measurable monotone convergence for arbitrary
uncountable nets.
\end{proof}

For the actual majorants of any normalized $u\in\EE$, the costs
$R-u_i$ are nonnegative bounded continuous on $U$, increase there
to $R-u$, and have finite $\nu$ integral. Lemma~\ref{radon} and
decreasing energy continuity show
\[
 E(u_i)+I_\nu(u_i)\longrightarrow E(u)+I_\nu(u).             \tag{4}
\]
Thus taking the supremum only over actual normalized model envelopes
still gives exactly $D_\nu$. For each $k\geq1$ choose one such
$u_k$ with objective at least $D_\nu-1/k$.
This choice is a sequence of near maximizers of a real supremum;
it does not impose metrizability on $K$ or replace the defining nets.

The costs of these near maximizers are uniformly bounded. Indeed
$D_\nu\geq0$ because $R$ has objective zero. By (1) and linearity
of the relative integral on a genuine convex combination,
\[
 r I_\nu(u)-C_nr^2B(u)\leq D_\nu.
\]
At $r=1/(2C_n)$ this gives
\[
 I_\nu(u)\leq B(u)/2+2C_nD_\nu,\qquad
 E(u)+I_\nu(u)\leq-B(u)/2+2C_nD_\nu.                      \tag{5}
\]
Consequently every chosen $u_k$ has
$B(u_k)\leq4C_nD_\nu+2=:B_\nu$.
This is coercivity derived from the explicit contraction input;
bounded cost alone supplies no variational attainment.

\section{The same uniform variation estimate at every genuine base}
\begin{proposition}\label{variation}
Under items1--4, (2) extends with the same $B,c,h,K_c,t_c,A_h(B)$
to every normalized genuine $u\in\EE$ with $B(u)\leq B$:
\[
 \left|E(P_\theta(u+th))-E(u)-t\int h\,dM(u)\right|
 \leq K_ct^2/2+|t|A_h(B)/c.                                \tag{6}
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Take its actual nonpositive model majorants $f_i$ from item1.
Their envelope costs are at most $B$, so (2) holds uniformly for
all $i$ with the same constants. The perturbed envelopes lie between
$u-|t|\|h\|_\infty$ and $u+|t|\|h\|_\infty$ at their endpoint,
and hence have finite genuine energy. At fixed $t$, their energies
decrease to $E(P_\theta(u+th))$ by item1. The unperturbed energies
decrease to $E(u)$, and $\int h\,dM(u_i)\to\int h\,dM(u)$
by item3. Taking this limit in (2) proves (6).
There is no passage of a derivative through the net: the entire
uniform finite increment estimate passes at fixed $t$ first.
\end{proof}

\section{Approximate stationarity gives the target before attainment}
\begin{theorem}\label{approx}
Under items1--4, every target (3) is a weak limit of actual outputs
$M(u_k)$ of normalized model-envelope near maximizers. Their costs
are bounded by $B_\nu$, and no actual maximizing potential is
assumed to exist.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Fix one rational model $h$. Write $\epsilon_k=1/k$ and
$z_{k,t}=P_\theta(u_k+th)$. This is a genuine finite-energy
potential by the bounds in Proposition~\ref{variation}. Its generic
value is finite; normalize it when applying (3). Raw energy and mass
make the objective invariant under that constant shift.
The obstacle inequality $z_{k,t}\leq u_k+th$ gives, on $U$,
\[
 I_\nu(z_{k,t})\geq I_\nu(u_k)-t\int h\,d\nu.
\]
All terms are finite by (3), and the near-maximizer inequality yields
\[
 E(z_{k,t})-E(u_k)-t\int h\,d\nu\leq\epsilon_k.             \tag{7}
\]
It is essential that the perturbed obstacle here is $u_k+th$,
rather than an arbitrary larger model majorant: the latter would
introduce an uncontrolled integral against $\nu$.

Use (6) at the cost bound $B_\nu$ for both signs of $t$, with
fixed $c>B_\nu/V$. For positive $t<t_c$ it gives
\[
 \left|\int h\,d(M(u_k)-\nu)\right|
 \leq\epsilon_k/t+K_ct/2+A_h(B_\nu)/c.                    \tag{8}
\]
First send $k\to\infty$ at fixed $c,t$, then $t\downarrow0$
for this fixed $c$, and finally $c\to\infty$.
Both one-sided integral limits coincide with $\int h\,d\nu$.
Original uniform model density and the common raw mass $V$ give
the same limit for every $h\in C(K)$. This is weak convergence of
the whole chosen sequence on the original compact carrier.
No compact-cluster maximizer or fixed-target strong integration
has been used.
\end{proof}

\section{Optional fixed-test integration consequence}
The following needs the additional, explicitly conditional ordered-gap
tail package proposed in the completed partial paper. For every
normalized $v\in\EE$, set $b_v=R-v$ on $U$ and zero on $Z$.
For every cost bound $B$ and $\eta>0$ assume that an actual
$a_\eta\in C(K)$ satisfies
\[
 0\leq a_\eta\leq b_v,\quad a_\eta|_Z=0,\qquad
 \sup_{B(u)\leq B}\int(b_v-a_\eta)\,dM(u)<\eta.             \tag{9}
\]
The proposed construction first fixes a model majorant of $v$ using
its ordered energy gap, then fixes a continuous Kodaira collar using
the uniform algebraic-cap estimate. This fixes both choices before
any output index. Formula (9) is stronger than a bounded first moment.

\begin{proposition}\label{integration}
If (9) holds, the output sequence in Theorem~\ref{approx} satisfies,
for every fixed genuine $v\in\EE$ and $h\in C(K)$,
\[
 \int h(R-v)\,dM(u_k)\longrightarrow\int h(R-v)\,d\nu.     \tag{10}
\]
The family consisting of these outputs and $\nu$ has uniform
integrable tails for this fixed relative test.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
On $U$, $b_v$ is nonnegative lsc, since $R$ is continuous and $v$
is usc. Assigning zero on $Z$ gives a global nonnegative lsc
function. Thus $b_v-a_\eta$ is nonnegative lsc on $K$.
Weak Radon Portmanteau, valid on compact Hausdorff $K$, and (9) give
\[
 \int(b_v-a_\eta)\,d\nu
       \leq\liminf_k\int(b_v-a_\eta)\,dM(u_k)\leq\eta.
\]
The target is algebraically null, so this is the actual relative
integral in (3), without hiding values on reference poles.
The integral of the fixed continuous $h a_\eta$ passes weakly.
Both error terms are at most $\|h\|_\infty\eta$.
Let $\eta\downarrow0$ to prove (10).
If $C=\|a_\eta\|_\infty$, then
$b_v\mathbf1_{\{b_v>2C\}}\leq2|b_v-a_\eta|$.
Choose $\eta$ first and then this fixed threshold to prove uniform
tails over the stated family. Shifts of $v$ use the raw mass law.
\end{proof}

Theorem~\ref{approx} places every intrinsic target in a weak closure
of a bounded-cost actual output family. Proposition~\ref{integration}
then gives convergence for each fixed genuine test. Neither assertion
controls a simultaneously changing test $u_k$ against $\nu$, or makes
$E(u_k)+I_\nu(u_k)$ attain its supremum at a genuine cluster.
Strict concavity, a genuine strong-completeness argument and exclusion
of all energy/integral jumps are still required. Identification of
all mixed unbounded moving products, strict Borel comparison and
uniqueness of every solution also remain open.

\section{Absolute-value contraction with every multiplicity}
Let $Y\to Z\times\mathbb P^1$ be a smooth SNC equivariant model, product

\begin{lemma}[Graph identity]\label{graph}
With $c_{ij}=b_ib_j(E_iE_j\Gamma)$ for $i<j$, one has
\begin{equation}\label{graph-eq}
 -D^2\Gamma=\sum_{i<j}c_{ij}(a_i-a_j)^2,\qquad c_{ij}\geq0.
\end{equation}
For every rational continuous model function $f$,
\begin{equation}\label{abs-contract}
 \|\,|f|\,\|_\Gamma^2\leq\|f\|_\Gamma^2,
 \qquad\|f_D\|_\Gamma^2=-D^2\Gamma.
\end{equation}
The same contraction holds for a rational Lipschitz piecewise linear
function $P(f)$ of Lipschitz constant one, provided it is represented by
the corresponding resolved model function.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The line bundle $\OO(F)$ restricts trivially to each $E_i$. Hence
$\sum_j b_j(E_iE_j\Gamma)=0$ for every $i$. For $i\ne j$, $E_iE_j$ is
an effective SNC stratum, and the relatively nef $N_l$ restrict to nef
bundles on this projective vertical stratum. Thus its intersection is
nonnegative. Expanding $D^2\Gamma$, replacing its diagonal terms with
the preceding zero-row identities, and collecting unordered pairs proves
\eqref{graph-eq}. This derivation includes the diagonal coefficients,
the $b_i$, and every exceptional component.

Resolve the absolute value \emph{before} applying the graph identity.
Choose integral $q$ clearing $D$ and rational $C$ sufficiently large that
$q(CF+D)$ and $q(CF-D)$ are effective integral vertical Cartier divisors.
Principalize the invariant ideal
\[

\]
On a dominating SNC model it is $\OO(-G)$, and $CF-G/q$ represents
$|f_D|$: its semivaluative coefficient is
$C-\min(C+f_D,C-f_D)=|f_D|$.
The ideal is the unit ideal off the central fiber; no horizontal poles
are introduced. On every central component of this refined model the

pulled $D$. Pull back all $N_l$ and $F$, retaining their new central

by $C_n\sqrt{b_jd_A(\tau,\rho)}\leq C'_n\sqrt{b_jb}$.
The quadratic forms are nonnegative by Lemma~\ref{graph}; hence their
polarizations satisfy Cauchy--Schwarz. If $a\leq b$, induction gives
$b_j\leq C_na^{2^{-j}}b^{1-2^{-j}}$. If $a>b$, use $b_{n-1}\leq4b$.
This proves the single repeated-slot estimate.

For a third potential $\zeta$, apply that estimate to both differences
$\xi-\zeta$ and $\zeta-\eta$ in the average $T_\tau^{n-1}$.
Quasi-convexity and the average formula yield
$d\leq C_nb^\beta\max(d,b)^{1-\beta}$, where
$d=d_A(\xi,\eta)$ and $b=\max(d_A(\xi,\zeta),d_A(\eta,\zeta))$.
If $d\geq b$ divide by $d^{1-\beta}$; otherwise the conclusion is
immediate. Thus $d_A$ satisfies a dimension-only quasi-triangle bound.
Average all the desired $\rho_l$. Expanding its $(n-1)$st power
dominates each nonnegative mixed quadratic form, and the repeated-slot
bound, quasi-convexity, quasi-triangle bound, and \eqref{J-formula}
give \eqref{slotbound}. When $n=1$, there is one empty-slot seminorm
and the assertion is immediate with $\beta=1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Absolute finite moment]\label{absolute-finite}
Set $\alpha=2^{-n}$ and
$B_* =\max(J_A(\xi),J_A(\eta),J_A(\psi))$.
Then
\begin{equation}\label{absolute-finite-eq}
 \int|\xi-\eta|\,d\MA_{A,\rm raw}(\psi)
 \leq |\xi(v_0)-\eta(v_0)|V_A
      +C_n\delta_A(\xi,\eta)^\alpha
         J_A(\psi)^{1/2}B_*^{1/2-\alpha}.
\end{equation}
This assertion includes $V_A=0$, with no division by volume.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Let $g=|\xi-\eta|$ and resolve it as in Lemma~\ref{graph}. Since the
trivial metric has measure $V_A\delta_{v_0}$, telescoping from $j=0$ gives
\[
 \int g\,d(\MA_A(\psi)-\MA_A(0))
  =\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}(0,g)(0,\psi)T_\psi^jT_0^{n-1-j}.
\]
Bound each term by Cauchy--Schwarz. The first seminorm is at most the
one for $\xi-\eta$ by \eqref{abs-contract}, and \eqref{slotbound}
controls it. The second is at most $C_nJ_A(\psi)^{1/2}$ by
\eqref{J-formula}. Use \eqref{midbound} and sum the $n$ terms.
This proves \eqref{absolute-finite-eq}. Constants have zero quadratic
form, so no normalization changes the estimate. If $V_A=0$, positivity
and mass force the top measure to be zero already. Zero-factor cases
are read by continuity; for $n=1$ the last factor has exponent zero
and is omitted.
\end{proof}

\section{Independent uniform finite-model variation}\label{variation-section}
In this section $L$ is any of the retained actual big rational bundles.
Let $Y\to X\times\mathbb P^1$ be a smooth equivariant modification,
product away from zero, $F=\sum b_EE$, and $D$ an actual vertical
rational Cartier divisor. Write $f=f_D$ and $d=n+1$.
The full relative section lattice, for $R_m=H^0(X,mL)$, is
\begin{equation}\label{lattice}
 \Lambda_m=\bigoplus_j t^{-w_{mj}}k[t]s_{mj},\qquad
 ma\leq w_{mj}\leq mb
\end{equation}
when $aF\leq D\leq bF$. Indeed divisor comparison gives
$t^{-ma}R_m[t]\subset\Lambda_m\subset t^{-mb}R_m[t]$;
equivariance grades this lattice and an adapted basis of its finite
homogeneous flag gives \eqref{lattice}. Proper normal birational section
descent retains the \emph{whole} original $R_m$. No finite generation
of the section ring is assumed. Gluing to the product lattice at infinity gives
\begin{equation}\label{dimformula}
 h^0(Y,m(\rho_X^*L+D+cF))
          =\sum_j\max(w_{mj}+mc+1,0).
\end{equation}
For sufficiently large rational $c$, this is $(mc+1)\dim R_m+\sum_jw_{mj}$.
Section-volume limits therefore give an intrinsic eventual intercept
\begin{equation}\label{intercept}
 \vol_Y(\rho_X^*L+D+cF)/d=cV+\mathscr E(f).
\end{equation}
The full-section lattice shows that $\mathscr E$ is invariant under
model refinement, monotone, $V$-translation equivariant, and
$V$-Lipschitz for the original sup norm. Ordinary volume-root concavity,
applied to \eqref{intercept} and expanded at $c\to\infty$, makes it
concave on rational model functions. It has a unique Lipschitz extension
to $C(K)$ by actual ample model density from G0.

BFJ volume differentiation on this \emph{big algebraic} $(n+1)$-fold gives,
for large $c$,
\begin{equation}\label{finite-mu}
 \mu_D=\sum_E b_E\langle(\rho_X^*L+D+cF)^n\rangle\cdot E\,\delta_{v_E},
 \quad \mu_D(K)=V,\quad D\mathscr E_f(h)=\int h\,d\mu_D.
\end{equation}
Every coefficient is nonnegative by the volume derivative in the effective
$E$ direction. Each is independent of sufficiently large $c$, by
differentiating \eqref{intercept} in $D+sE$ on a common eventual half-line.
The derivative in $F$ gives the mass. Refinement is compatible: an
effective exceptional prime $G$ has $p_*\OO(rG)=\OO$ for $r\geq0$;
adding it to a pulled bundle does not change sections. The derivative
coefficient there is zero. Projection and pullback retain the other
coefficients. Equivalently the original functional and its model
derivatives are unchanged. This constructs finite model measures, not
an unbounded original operator.

\begin{lemma}[Positive deficient measures]\label{deficient}
Suppose $f_D\leq0$ and $\mathscr E(f_D)\geq-B$, $B\geq0$.
For every $c>B/V$, the class $\alpha_D(c)=\rho_X^*L+D+cF$ is big, and
\begin{equation}\label{deficient-eq}
 0\leq\mu_{D,c}:=\sum_Eb_E\langle\alpha_D(c)^n\rangle\cdot E\,\delta_{v_E}
 \leq\mu_D,\qquad (\mu_D-\mu_{D,c})(K)\leq B/c.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Set $g_D(c)=\vol(\alpha_D(c))/d$. Formula \eqref{dimformula} gives
a convex function of $c$, with $g_D(0)=0$, slope bounded by $V$,
eventual expression $cV+\mathscr E(f_D)$, and
$g_D(c)\geq cV+\mathscr E(f_D)$. For $c>B/V$ this is positive,
so the actual bundle is big. At that point BFJ differentiation gives
$g_D'(c)=\mu_{D,c}(K)$. Convexity gives
$g_D'(c)\geq g_D(c)/c\geq V-B/c$, and its eventual slope gives
$g_D'(c)\leq V$.

The coefficient assertion requires more than this mass bound. The full
filtered-space trace in \eqref{dimformula} gives
\[
 T_D(c):=\mathscr E(f_D)+cV-g_D(c)
       =\lim_m\frac{n!}{m^{n+1}}\sum_j\min(w_{mj}+mc,0).
\]
Terms arising from the $+1$ in \eqref{dimformula} tend to zero, since
$\dim R_m=O(m^n)$. Increasing an effective vertical divisor increases
each ordered weight of its full lattice: this follows from inclusion
of every filtration space, or its dimension distribution. Thus each
finite trace of the increasing function $\min(x+mc,0)$ increases.
The same is true of $T_D(c)$. Its derivative in each effective $E$
is nonnegative and equals the coefficient of $\mu_D-\mu_{D,c}$
divided by $b_E$. This proves coefficientwise positivity.
Together with the mass estimate it proves \eqref{deficient-eq}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform finite-model Taylor estimate]\label{taylor}
Fix a rational original model direction $h$, a cost bound $B$, and
$c>B/V$. There exist $K_c<\infty$ and $t_c>0$, independent of the
nonpositive obstacle $f_D$ and of its refinement, such that
\begin{equation}\label{taylor-eq}
 |\mathscr E(f_D+th)-\mathscr E(f_D)-t\int h\,d\mu_D|
 \leq K_ct^2/2+|t|\|h\|_\infty(2B+2V\|h\|_\infty)/c
\end{equation}
whenever $\mathscr E(f_D)\geq-B$ and $|t|<t_c$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Represent $h$ by a signed vertical Cartier $H$ on one fixed smooth
determination $Z$. Choose an actual ample $T$ there, and refine to carry
each $D$, always pulling $T,H$ back. Let
$\gamma=\rho_X^*L+cF$, $\alpha=\alpha_D(c)$,
$\kappa=d(cV-B)>0$, and $M=d\langle\gamma^n\rangle\cdot T$.
We have $\alpha\leq\gamma$ in psef order and $\vol(\alpha)\geq\kappa$.
While $\alpha-rT$ stays big, volume differentiation and positive-product
monotonicity bound its volume loss by $rM$. Thus
$\alpha-r_0T$ is big for $r_0=\kappa/[2(M+1)]$: a first earlier exit
would contradict volume continuity and the remaining positive volume.
The constants are unchanged under refinement, since their tests live on $Z$.

Choose $a>0$ with $aT\pm H$ nef and put $\lambda=a/r_0$.
Then $\lambda\alpha\pm H$ are psef. For $|s|\lambda<1/2$, positivity
and monotonicity sandwich
\[
 (1-\lambda|s|)^n\langle\alpha^n\rangle
 \leq\langle(\alpha+sH)^n\rangle
 \leq(1+\lambda|s|)^n\langle\alpha^n\rangle.
\]
To pair with $H$, decompose it into the \emph{two fixed nef tests}
$H_1=aT+H$, $H_2=aT$. Their pairings are bounded by
$\langle\gamma^n\rangle\cdot H_l$, fixed before the model varies.
The sandwich implies a common Lipschitz bound on the derivative of
$\vol(\alpha+sH)/d$. Integrating gives
\[
 |g_{D+tH}(c)-g_D(c)-t\int h\,d\mu_{D,c}|\leq K_ct^2/2.
\]
No signed test is inserted into an effective-order inequality.

Put $H_0=\|h\|_\infty$. At parameter $s$, use the nonpositive obstacle
$f_D+sh-|s|H_0$ and time parameter $c_s=c+|s|H_0$. Its cost is at
most $B_s=B+2V|s|H_0$, by the actual Lipschitz and constant laws.
Crucially choose $t_c\leq1$ and, if $H_0>0$,
$t_c<(c-B/V)/(2H_0)$. Then $c_s>B_s/V$ for both signs throughout
the integration path. The rough fixed bound $B+2VH_0$ alone would
not justify this big-cone condition when $c$ is near $B/V$.
Its deficient class is exactly $\alpha+sH$. Its full derivative measure
is unchanged by the scalar shift. Lemma~\ref{deficient} bounds the
positive derivative tail by $B_s/c_s\leq(B+2VH_0)/c$.
Integrate the $h$-derivative along this path and replace the initial
deficient derivative by $\mu_D$, at extra cost $|t|H_0B/c$.
The resulting sum is \eqref{taylor-eq}. The finite-model energy is $C^1$
on the path, since one sufficiently large time twist realizes its
intercept in a common neighborhood of actual big classes. This proves
the integration for both signs. When $H_0=0$ there is nothing to prove.
\end{proof}

Theorem~\ref{taylor} verifies the \emph{finite-model} variation ingredient.
It does not itself construct the scalar outer energy on every genuine base,
prove its envelope identity, construct a weakly continuous unbounded output,
or identify weighted moving products. Those distinctions are retained next.

\section{Explicit unresolved original-carrier antecedents}\label{package}
The rest of the positive-volume conclusions are conditional on the following
package S--M. It is stated for the \emph{entire} retained domain of Section 1,
with the literal single-net cone; no narrower space is substituted.
We do not claim to have proved the entire package independently.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[S1.] That cone is convex, finite-max closed and decreasing closed at
finite generic endpoints. Its normalized space is compact in the topology
of pointwise convergence at rational divisorial valuations. Each upper
bounded usc obstacle with a genuine generically finite minorant has a
genuine all-point envelope. The minimal reference is $R=P_\theta(0)$,
$R(v_0)=0$, and every normalized genuine $u$ satisfies $u\leq R\leq0$.
\item[S2.] The scalar energy on the \emph{whole} genuine cone is
\[
 E(u)=\inf_{f\in C(K),\ f\geq u}\mathscr E(f),\quad
 \E^1_\theta=\{u\in\PSH(\theta):E(u)>-\infty\},\quad B(u)=-E(u)
\]
for normalized $u$. It is concave, monotone, weakly usc, decreasing-net
continuous, has $E(R)=0$ and $E(u+c)=E(u)+cV$, and satisfies
$E(P_\theta(f))=\mathscr E(f)$ for continuous obstacles. Every normalized
$u\in\E^1_\theta$ has decreasing nonpositive rational model majorants
$f_i\downarrow u$ with $f_i(v_0)=0$, whose envelopes $a_i=P_\theta(f_i)$
decrease all-point to $u$ and whose energies decrease to $E(u)$.
For fixed $h\in C(K)$, their perturbed envelopes decrease to
$P_\theta(u+th)$ at each fixed $t$. Outer energy on usc obstacles equals
the energy of this envelope. Its continuous-obstacle value is the
full-section trace constructed from $W_m(f;s)$ below.
\item[S3.] There is an actual Kodaira identity $L=aA+E_0$ with $a>0$,
$A$ ample and $E_0\geq0$. Write $Z=E_0^\an$, $U=K\setminus Z$.
There is a normalized actual $w_Z\in\E^1_\theta$ with $w_Z=-\infty$
on $Z$. Genuine relative contraction holds with a dimension constant
$C_0\geq1$:
\[
 B((1-r)R+ru)\leq C_0r^2B(u),\qquad 0<r<1.
\]
\item[M1.] A target-independent map $M$ on every actual $\E^1_\theta$
has positive original Radon outputs of raw mass $V$, constant invariance,
and $M(P_\theta(f_D))=\mu_D$ from \eqref{finite-mu}.
For the canonical majorants in S2, $M(a_i)\to M(u)$ weakly on $K$.
Every such output gives $Z$ zero mass. The map is not defined using an
inverse target construction.
\item[M2.] For any fixed finite list of normalized nonpositive rational
model obstacles, resolve the \emph{full} $|mL|$ system and their full
relative lattices on common smooth equivariant models. One has the
actual generic identity $p_m^*L=A_m+T_m$, with $mA_m$ generated,
$mT_m$ effective, and bounded relatively nef model scalars $\psi_{m,D}$
on this \emph{same actual} $A_m$, such that
\[
 \phi_{m,D}=q_{T_m}+\psi_{m,D},\quad\phi_{m,0}=q_{T_m},\quad
 A_m^n\to V,\quad e_{A_m}(\psi_{m,D})\to E(P_\theta(f_D)),\quad
 \psi_{m,D}(v_0)\to0.
\]
These full complete-system stages are minorants of their original
envelopes. Their pushed auxiliary raw top measures converge to $\mu_D$.
All degree limits are cofinal divisibility limits with nonempty systems.
The auxiliary bounded nef trace agrees with the finite intersection
energy $e_{A_m}$. Multiplication by $s_{\ell T_m}$ injects
$H^0(X_m,\ell A_m)$ into the \emph{full original} $H^0(X,\ell L)$
in cleared degrees. No assertion of original $\E^1$ membership is made
for the physical functions $q_{T_m}+\psi_{m,D}$.
\end{enumerate}
Here M2 is only a finite-list, finite-obstacle compatibility assertion.
It does not assume an unbounded mixed product, arbitrary approximation
independence, attainment, comparison, whole supporting planes, or separation.
Theorem~\ref{taylor} supplies its finite variation ingredient; no further
uniform Taylor hypothesis is hidden in S--M.

The supplied scalar constructions and moving-product arguments suggest
S--M, but checking all their antecedents and unbounded passages is separate
work. In particular G1 alone does not grant S1, and G0 does not grant M1
on a big nonnef class. The conditional theorem below will show exactly
what follows if this package is established.

\section{Independent bounded-obstacle density and directed integration}
The density result in this section requires only the single-net definition,
genuine obstacle envelopes from S1, and ordinary Kodaira/ample background.
It reconstructs the bounded ingredient of the supplied ROOT198 bridge.
Let $W=q_{E_0}\leq0$. It is finite continuous on $U$, and tensoring its
single section with a weight-zero generating system of $aA$ realizes it
as an actual FS scalar on $L$.

For $f\in C(K)$ and nonzero $s\in H^0(X,mL)$ put
\[
 W_m(f;s)=\inf_K(mf-\log\|s\|),
 \qquad
 \phi_{m,f}=m^{-1}\max_j(\log\|s_{mj}\|+\lfloor W_m(f;s_{mj})\rfloor).
\]
At a section zero the bracket is $+\infty$. Its bounds are
$m\min f\leq W_m(f;s)\leq m f(v_0)$. Superlevel subspaces of the
full section space form a finite closed-endpoint flag; choose an adapted
basis. The ultrametric inequality over trivial $k$ makes $\phi_{m,f}$
basis independent. Powers of sections and superadditivity of weights
make these stages increase in divisibility order. In the model case
they are exactly the complete relative-lattice stages by the all-point
section-extension calculation in G1. Real FS weights are dominated in
the supremum: raising a degree-$r$ section to its $\ell$th power loses
less than $1/(r\ell)$ upon flooring its weight.

\begin{lemma}[Actual bounded density]\label{density}
If $u_f=P_\theta(f)$ is genuine, then
\[
 u_f=\sup_m\phi_{m,f}\quad\text{on }U.
\]
This envelope is finite continuous on $U$ and the stages converge
uniformly on each compact subset of $U$. For $|f|\leq C$, the relative
function $u_f-R$ is bounded by $C$ on $U$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Take $C$ a positive integer with $|f|\leq C$. The genuine minorant
$W-C$ makes $u_f$ finite on $U$. Given a defining net $h_i\downarrow u_f$
on actual $B_i$, fix rational $0<t<1$ and $\epsilon>0$ \emph{before}
taking a tail. The actual difference
\[
 L-(1-t)B_i-t(L-aA)
\]
is eventually ample, since its numerical class tends to $ta[A]$.
Compactness of the nested closed sets $\{h_i\geq f+\epsilon\}$ gives
a tail with $h_i<f+\epsilon$ on \emph{all} of $K$, including supported
poles. Tensor with a generated system of that actual ample difference.
The scalar $(1-t)(h_i-\epsilon)+t(W-C)$ is then an actual FS function
on $L$ below $f$ everywhere. At $x\in U$, let $i$ tend to its endpoint,
then $t\downarrow0$, then $\epsilon\downarrow0$. Full-system domination
including the real-weight flooring observation proves the reverse
inequality $u_f\leq\sup_m\phi_{m,f}$. The other inequality follows
because each stage is a genuine minorant.

One cleared Kodaira-section tensor degree has no common zeros on $U$.
For all its multiples the stages are finite continuous there; their
supremum is lsc, while the genuine envelope is usc. Thus equality makes
it continuous. On a fixed compact subset the decreasing continuous gaps
to this envelope have empty positive-margin superlevel intersections.
Compactness yields uniform convergence for the divisibility-directed
stages. Finally constant shifts and envelope order give
$R-C\leq u_f\leq R+C$ on $U$. No equality on $Z$ is asserted.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Bounded weighted passage]\label{bounded-passage}
If positive Radon measures $\sigma_i\to\sigma$ weakly on $K$ with
converging masses, $\sigma(Z)=0$, and $b$ is bounded continuous on $U$,
then its bounded extension by zero on $Z$ has converging integrals.
The same holds for bounded changing section quotients which converge
uniformly to $b$ on every compact subset of $U$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Choose a compact $F\subset U$ with arbitrarily small omitted $\sigma$
mass. By compact Hausdorff normality choose a continuous $0\leq\chi\leq1$,
equal to one on $F$ with compact support in $U$. The product $\chi b$
extends continuously by zero on $K$. Pass that fixed continuous integral
through weak convergence. Bound each omitted part by the common bound
times $\sigma_i(K)-\int\chi d\sigma_i$, which tends to its arbitrarily
small limiting value. For changing quotients first fix this collar,
then their uniform error on its support, and only then take the index.
This proves the claim without indicators of changing Borel sets or
uniform convergence at polar points.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Radon finite-cover lemma]\label{radon}
Let $c_i\geq0$ be a directed increasing net of continuous functions on
$U$, and let $\nu$ be finite Radon on $K$ with $\nu(Z)=0$.
Then $\int_U\sup_i c_i\,d\nu=\sup_i\int_U c_i\,d\nu$,
allowing $+\infty$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For $a>0$, the open set $\{\sup_i c_i>a\}$ is the union of the open
superlevels of the $c_i$. Each compact subset has a finite subcover;
directedness gives one index dominating that finite set. Radon inner
regularity identifies the superlevel mass with the supremum of these
masses. Finitely many threshold masses can be approached simultaneously
by a common index. Use finite lower layer-cake step sums for the cap
$\min(\sup_i c_i,N)$, refine the threshold mesh, then let $N\to\infty$.
The reverse inequality follows from pointwise order. This proves the
net integral assertion; measurable monotone convergence for arbitrary
uncountable nets was not used.
\end{proof}

\section{Reconstruction of arbitrary-target output approximation}\label{target-approx}
For a normalized actual $u\in\E^1_\theta$, all differences below are
taken where $R$ is finite. An intrinsic target is a positive original
Radon measure $\nu$ with
\begin{equation}\label{target}
 \begin{aligned}
 &\nu(K)=V,\qquad\nu\{R=-\infty\}=0,\\
 &I_\nu(u)=\int(R-u)d\nu<\infty\quad\text{for every actual }u\in\E^1_\theta,\\
 &D_\nu=\sup_{u(v_0)=0}\{E(u)+I_\nu(u)\}<\infty.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The redundant integrability clause is displayed to retain every actual
test: finite dual energy directly forces each integral to be finite.
No absolute integrability of $R$ is imposed. S3 and $w_Z$ give
$\nu(Z)=0$, since its relative cost is infinite on $Z$ outside the
already excluded reference poles. These are intrinsic targets of the
specified reference, not a support-restricted class.

\begin{proposition}[Same fixed increment at every genuine base]\label{fixed-increment}
Under S--M, \eqref{taylor-eq} holds with its same constants at every
normalized genuine $u$ of cost at most $B$, replacing its left side by
\[
 |E(P_\theta(u+th))-E(u)-t\int h\,dM(u)|.
\]
Both derivative signs exist for every original $h\in C(K)$ and equal
$\int h\,dM(u)$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Apply Theorem~\ref{taylor} to the S2 model majorants $f_i$. Their
envelope costs are at most $B$. At fixed $t$, the perturbed envelopes
and their energies decrease to those of $P_\theta(u+th)$, and M1
passes the fixed continuous $h$ integral. Thus the whole finite
increment estimate passes with unchanged constants. There is no
exchange of a derivative with a net. Divide by $t$ with both signs,
first let $t\to0$ at fixed $c>B/V$, then $c\to\infty$.
Uniform model approximation of any original continuous $h$ changes
the divided energy increment and the measure integral by at most
$V$ times its sup-norm error. Fix the approximation before $t\to0$,
then let this error tend to zero. This proves both continuous signs.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Output approximation before attainment]\label{output-approx}
Under S--M, every target \eqref{target} has normalized model-envelope
near-maximizers $u_k$ with
\[
 E(u_k)+I_\nu(u_k)\geq D_\nu-1/k,\quad
 B(u_k)\leq Q_\nu:=4C_0D_\nu+2,\quad M(u_k)\to\nu\text{ weakly}.
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
For the actual majorants $a_i$ of any $u$, the costs $R-a_i$ are
nonnegative bounded continuous on $U$ by Lemma~\ref{density}, increase
to $R-u$, and have finite $\nu$ integral. Lemma~\ref{radon} and S2
show convergence of the objective. Its supremum over model envelopes
is therefore exactly $D_\nu$. Choose a sequence within $1/k$ of that
real supremum; this does not impose metrizability on $K$.

Reference contraction gives
$rI_\nu(u)-C_0r^2B(u)\leq D_\nu$. At $r=1/(2C_0)$ it gives
$I_\nu(u)\leq B(u)/2+2C_0D_\nu$. The near-maximizer lower bound
then gives $B(u_k)\leq Q_\nu$.

For a fixed rational model $h$, perturb the \emph{actual base}
$u_k+th$, not its larger physical model obstacle. Its envelope $z_{k,t}$
lies between $u_k\pm|t|\|h\|_\infty$ and is actual finite energy by S2.
The obstacle inequality gives
$I_\nu(z_{k,t})\geq I_\nu(u_k)-t\int h\,d\nu$.
Normalize it only when using \eqref{target}; the raw constant law and
mass keep the objective unchanged. Near maximality implies
\[
 E(z_{k,t})-E(u_k)-t\int h\,d\nu\leq1/k.
\]
Proposition~\ref{fixed-increment} at bound $Q_\nu$, with both signs,
gives for $0<t<t_c$
\[
 \left|\int h\,d(M(u_k)-\nu)\right|
 \leq \frac1{kt}+K_ct/2+
           \|h\|_\infty(2Q_\nu+2V\|h\|_\infty)/c.
\]
Send $k\to\infty$ at fixed $c,t$, then $t\downarrow0$ at that $c$,
then $c\to\infty$. Uniform model density and the common raw mass
extend convergence to every continuous test. This independently
reconstructs the conditional ROOT199 bridge, before attainment.
\end{proof}

\section{Midpoint transfer with the lost-volume error retained}\label{transfer}
For normalized genuine $a,b$ define the scalar midpoint defect
\[
 \delta(a,b)=E((a+b)/2)-(E(a)+E(b))/2\geq0.
\]
The central new original-carrier assertion of this paper is the following
\emph{conditional} absolute estimate.

\begin{theorem}[Absolute midpoint modulus]\label{absolute-original}
Assume S--M. For any normalized $a,b,w\in\E^1_\theta$,
\begin{equation}\label{modulus-output}
 \int_U|a-b|\,dM(w)
 \leq C_n\delta(a,b)^\alpha B(w)^{1/2}
           \max\{B(a),B(b),B(w)\}^{1/2-\alpha},\quad \alpha=2^{-n}.
\end{equation}
Every genuine relative test is integrable for $M(w)$, and these outputs
have finite intrinsic dual energy. For any target \eqref{target},
\begin{equation}\label{modulus-target}
 \int_U|a-b|\,d\nu
 \leq C_n\delta(a,b)^\alpha Q_\nu^{1/2}
          \max\{B(a),B(b),Q_\nu\}^{1/2-\alpha}.
\end{equation}
All these integrals use original actual functions and relative values.
For unbounded pairs the absolute difference is defined where both relative

\section{Finite geometry: an absolute value contraction}
Let $A$ be an actual nef rational bundle on a smooth projective
$n$-fold, $n\geq1$, over an algebraically closed trivially valued
characteristic-zero field. Work first only with bounded rational
relatively nef model scalars on its original analytic carrier.
On a smooth common determination $\mathcal X$ the central fiber is
$F=\sum_i b_iE_i$ with SNC support; all $b_i$ are retained.
Write $T_\xi=(A,\xi)$ for a nef model slot,
$e_A(\xi)=T_\xi^{n+1}/(n+1)$ and
$J_A(\xi)=V_A\xi(v_0)-e_A(\xi)$, $V_A=A^n$.
The raw measure has coefficients $b_i(T_\xi|_{E_i})^n$ and mass
$V_A$. For a vertical scalar $f$ define
\[
 Q_\Gamma(f)=-(0,f)^2\Gamma,\qquad
 \Gamma=T_1\cdots T_{n-1},
\]
where the slots are nef on all central components.
For $n=1$ the product is empty. These are finite intersection
numbers; no unbounded ample estimate is imported.

\begin{lemma}[Graph contraction]\label{graph}
For a rational model function $f$, on a determination also realizing
the model function $|f|=\max(f,-f)$,
\[
 Q_\Gamma(|f|)\leq Q_\Gamma(f).                            \tag{1}
\]
More generally any scalar $1$-Lipschitz map on the finitely many
vertical values contracts the corresponding graph quadratic form.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
If $f_i$ is the value at $v_{E_i}$, its vertical divisor is
$D_f=\sum_i b_if_iE_i$. Set $c_{ij}=E_iE_j\Gamma$ for $i\ne j$.
SNC effectivity and nef restrictions give $c_{ij}\geq0$.
The restriction of the full fiber $F$ to each central component is
numerically trivial, so $\sum_j b_jE_iE_j\Gamma=0$.
Expanding the diagonal coefficients with this relation gives
\[
 -D_f^2\Gamma=\sum_{i<j}b_ib_jc_{ij}(f_i-f_j)^2.            \tag{2}
\]
Pulling slots and divisors to a further determination preserves
their finite intersections. The absolute-value model exists on an
actual vertical-ideal blowup: clear the denominators of $D_f$,
multiply the two fractional invertible ideals representing $f,-f$
by one sufficiently large power of the base parameter, take their
sum, and principalize it. The scalar logarithm of the norm of their
ideal sum is the maximum of the two scalar logarithms. Undoing the common parameter power
gives $\max(f,-f)$, with its value $|f_i|$ at every new divisorial
component. Characteristic-zero SNC resolution is ordinary algebraic
background; the generic fiber and original model scalars are retained.
Apply (2) on this common refinement and use
$||f_i|-|f_j||\leq|f_i-f_j|$. This proves (1).
The last assertion concerns the finite form (2); it asserts model
realizability only when the transformed values come from a model.
\end{proof}

Polarization of (2) gives Cauchy--Schwarz for $Q_\Gamma$.
The correct tangent identity, with $S=(0,\xi-\eta)$, is
\[
 T_\eta^{n+1}-T_\xi^{n+1}+(n+1)ST_\eta^n
 =-\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}(n-j)S^2T_\xi^jT_\eta^{n-1-j}.          \tag{3}
\]
Indeed telescope the first difference, subtract its tangent term,
and telescope each remaining difference once more; the term indexed
by $j$ occurs for $k=j+1,\ldots,n$.
In particular
\[
 J_A(\xi)=\frac1{n+1}\sum_{j<n}(n-j)
                     Q_{T_\xi^jT_0^{n-1-j}}(\xi).         \tag{4}
\]
The historically printed coefficient $j+1$ is not used with these
factor positions. All coefficients in (4) are positive.

\section{Finite slot estimates and an absolute integral}
Put $d_A(\xi,\eta)=\max_{j<n}Q_{T_\xi^jT_\eta^{n-1-j}}(\xi-\eta)$.
For completeness the finite slot-change argument is recalled.
Concavity of the finite energy follows by differentiating its
polynomial on a nef segment: its second derivative is
$-nQ_{T_{\xi_t}^{n-1}}(\xi-\eta)\leq0$.
The tangent remainder is therefore convex in its first variable;
by (3) it is comparable, with dimension constants, to $d_A$.
Expanding the average of two slots gives
\[
 d_A(\xi,\xi')\asymp_n
 Q_{T_{(\xi+\xi')/2}^{n-1}}(\xi-\xi').                    \tag{5}
\]
For $f=\xi-\xi'$, $\tau=(\xi+\xi')/2$, set
$a=d_A(\xi,\xi')$, $b=\max(d_A(\xi,\eta),d_A(\xi',\eta))$,
and $b_j=Q_{T_\eta^jT_\tau^{n-1-j}}(f)$.
Then $b_0\leq C_na$ and $b_{n-1}\leq4b$.
In $b_{j+1}-b_j$ split one occurrence of $f$ into
$T_\xi-T_\xi'$ and apply Cauchy--Schwarz separately with these
two nef slots. Since $2T_\tau-T_\xi=T_\xi'$ is nef and conversely,
their $f$ seminorms are at most $2b_j$; their other seminorms
are at most twice $d_A(\tau,\eta)\leq C_nb$ by convexity of the
tangent remainder. Thus
\[
 |b_{j+1}-b_j|\leq C_n\sqrt{b_jb}.
\]
Induction for $a\leq b$ gives
$b_j\leq C_na^{2^{-j}}b^{1-2^{-j}}$; for $a>b$ the final
bound $b_{n-1}\leq4b$ gives the same desired last-slot estimate.

To obtain the quasi-triangle estimate, split $\xi-\eta$ through a
third potential $\zeta$ in the average seminorm (5). Apply the
last-slot bound to the two differences. Convexity bounds the distances
from the averaged slot to $\zeta$ by
$C_n\max(d_A(\xi,\zeta),d_A(\eta,\zeta))$; its distances to
$\xi,\eta$ are bounded by $C_nd_A(\xi,\eta)$ by expansion.
Writing $d=d_A(\xi,\eta)$ and
$b=\max(d_A(\xi,\zeta),d_A(\eta,\zeta))$, this gives
$d\leq C_nb^{2^{1-n}}\max(d,b)^{1-2^{1-n}}$.
Divide by the power of $d$ when $d\geq b$; otherwise the conclusion
is immediate. Hence $d\leq C_nb$.
Average an arbitrary finite list of nef slots and expand its
nonnegative multinomial terms. The preceding last-slot bound,
quasi-triangle estimate and (4) then give
\[
 Q_{T_\psi^jT_0^{n-1-j}}(\xi-\eta)
 \leq C_n d_A(\xi,\eta)^{2^{1-n}}
       M^{1-2^{1-n}},\quad
 M=\max(J_A(\xi),J_A(\eta),J_A(\psi)).                    \tag{6}
\]
For $n=1$ there is one empty-slot seminorm and the same result
follows directly. Constants in the scalars affect neither these
seminorms nor $J_A$.

\begin{theorem}[Absolute raw finite estimate]\label{finiteabs}
For bounded rational relatively nef model scalars $\xi,\eta,\psi$,
with $\alpha=2^{-n}$,
\[
 \begin{split}
 \int|\xi-\eta|\,d\MA_{A,\mathrm{raw}}(\psi)
 \leq{}&V_A|\xi(v_0)-\eta(v_0)|\\
 &+C_n d_A(\xi,\eta)^\alpha J_A(\psi)^{1/2}
              M^{1/2-\alpha}.
 \end{split}                                             \tag{7}
\]
This includes $V_A=0$. There is no volume denominator.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Use the actual absolute-value model from Lemma~\ref{graph} and
telescope $T_\psi^n-T_0^n$. The difference between the integral
on the left and its trivial-model integral is
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^{n-1}(0,|\xi-\eta|)(0,\psi)T_\psi^jT_0^{n-1-j}.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz, (1), (6), and (4) bound its absolute value by
the second line of (7). The trivial measure is $V_A\delta_{v_0}$.
If an energy factor vanishes, use the seminorm formulas directly
or a finite polynomial limit. In dimension one the last exponent
is zero and the bound is $C_1d_A^{1/2}J_A(\psi)^{1/2}$.
If $V_A=0$, positivity and raw mass force the measure to be zero.
\end{proof}

\section{A quantitative finite midpoint defect}
Define the raw finite pairing
\[
 I_A(\xi,\eta)=\int(\xi-\eta)\,
       d(\MA_A(\eta)-\MA_A(\xi))
   =\sum_{j<n}Q_{T_\xi^jT_\eta^{n-1-j}}(\xi-\eta)\geq0.
\]
Thus $d_A\leq I_A$. Let $g(t)=e_A((1-t)\eta+t\xi)$.
Its second derivative is the negative of $n$ times
\[
 \sum_{j<n}\binom{n-1}{j}t^j(1-t)^{n-1-j}
                       Q_{T_\xi^jT_\eta^{n-1-j}}(\xi-\eta).
\]
The midpoint defect equals $\int_0^1G(t)(-g''(t))\,dt$, where
$G(t)=t/2$ for $t\leq1/2$ and $G(t)=(1-t)/2$ otherwise.
On $[1/4,3/4]$, $G\geq1/8$ and each power product is at least
$4^{-(n-1)}$. Consequently
\[
 e_A((\xi+\eta)/2)-\frac{e_A(\xi)+e_A(\eta)}2
       \geq c_n I_A(\xi,\eta),\qquad c_n=n4^{-(n+1)}>0.    \tag{8}
\]
This is elementary finite polynomial calculus, including nonreduced
fibers through (2). The constant need not be optimal.
